decks.name: LeetCode #253 - Meeting Rooms II
decks.description: Find minimum number of conference rooms required for all meetings

cards.question: Meeting Rooms II: Given an array of meeting time intervals intervals where intervals[i] = [starti, endi], return the minimum number of conference rooms required.

solutions.name: Min Heap
solutions.explanation: Sort intervals by start time. Use min heap to track end times of ongoing meetings. For each meeting, if earliest ending meeting (heap top) ends before current starts, reuse that room by removing from heap. Always add current meeting's end time to heap. Heap size represents rooms currently in use. Maximum heap size is answer. Greedy approach: always reuse earliest available room. O(n log n) time for sorting and heap operations.

solutions.name: Sweep Line Algorithm
solutions.explanation: Treat interval boundaries as events on timeline. Mark each start as +1 event (meeting begins) and each end as -1 event (meeting ends). Sort all event positions. Sweep through timeline accumulating event values to track active meeting count. Maximum count reached is answer. Classic computational geometry technique for interval overlap counting. O(n log n) time for sorting events.

solutions.name: Two Pointers
solutions.explanation: Separate meeting starts and ends into two sorted arrays. Use two pointers to process events chronologically. When processing start before end, meeting begins (increment count). When processing end before start, meeting ends (decrement count). Track maximum count reached. Elegant solution avoiding complex data structures. Similar to merge step in merge sort. O(n log n) time for sorting both arrays.

solutions.name: Greedy
solutions.explanation: Create explicit events for each interval boundary. Start event as (time, +1) and end event as (time, -1). Sort events by time, with tie-breaker: end events (-1) before start events (+1) at same time. Process events in order, accumulating count. Track maximum count reached. Tie-breaker ensures meeting ending frees room before meeting starting at same time can use it. Most explicit event-based solution. O(n log n) time for sorting events.
